Clinical/legal review remains required for emergency and collision guidance. The source conflicts on brake pumping and ABS behavior across physical118–121; do not teach its detailed procedures or a guarantee of stopping distance. Jump-start vent-cap and negative-terminal instructions, pressure-equalization/side-window escape details, child rescue sequence, impact bracing, choosing collision targets, fixed blowout speed and quantitative flood/float limits are withheld for vehicle-specific safety review. Physical116 age-specific phone wording differs from the later hands-free rule; preserve the currentness issue rather than imply one resolves the other. The move-over rule must retain safe-lane-change qualification from physical126. Dated teen and collision statistics remain unasserted; source-based first-aid detail is not a clinical training module. [A01] [A02] [A03] [A04] [A05] [A06] [A07] [A08] [A09] [A10] [A11] [A12]
Memory cue, authored product policy: “Remove distraction, keep control, get clear and call for help”. The cue retrieves complete cited rules and does not replace their conditions.
Terminology: ABS manages brake lockup; electronic stability control uses directional and traction information to intervene at individual wheels. Cognitive distraction remains possible with hands-free equipment.
Misconception to correct: Hands-free means attention-free, or moving over requires an unsafe lane change. The source keeps cognitive-distraction risk and allows slowing when a lane change cannot be safe.
